case_text:
Vignette:
A 38-year-old woman presents with a 3-week history of persistent throat clearing and a mild cough that is worse when lying down at night. She reports a sensation of mucus dripping in the back of her throat. She recently had a mild cold that resolved 4 weeks ago. She denies fever, facial pain, purulent nasal discharge, wheezing, or heartburn. She is a non-smoker. On examination, the oropharynx shows a cobblestone appearance of the posterior pharyngeal wall. Nasal mucosa is mildly erythematous with clear thin secretions. Lungs are clear to auscultation. There is no sinus tenderness on palpation.
